nodes.description: With reduced sodium current the muscle action potential is smaller and propagates less reliably along the sarcolemma, so contraction is driven less effectively and fiber force falls. This is a permanent deficit, unlike the episodic depolarization block of the dominant periodic paralyses.

nodes.description: Endplate potentials of normal size fail to trigger muscle action potentials because too few Nav1.4 channels are available at the endplate, a postsynaptic defect that leaves quantal release, acetylcholine receptor function and endplate structure intact. Enhanced use-dependent inactivation makes the failure worse during repetitive firing, which gives activity-dependent fatigability and a decremental response at higher stimulation rates. This is the main mechanism of the CMS16 presentation but is also seen in some myopathic patients.

nodes.description: Biallelic SCN4A variants reduce the sodium current carried by Nav1.4. Null alleles (nonsense, frameshift, essential splice and some missense, such as p.R104H, p.P382T and p.C1209F) abolish current; partial alleles reduce current amplitude or shift activation to more depolarized voltages; myasthenic alleles enhance fast inactivation or slow recovery from it, so fewer channels are available, especially during repetitive firing. In the null mouse the fetal isoform Nav1.5 does not compensate.
